title: Exploring the Limits of Zero Shot Vision Language Models for Hate Meme Detection: The Vulnerabilities and their Interpretations

bias_targets.methodology: Zero-shot classification of misogynistic memes using the MAMI dataset, combined with occlusion-based interpretability and error topic modeling to evaluate if models can detect implicit sexism, objectification, and female stereotyping.

Evaluating models on the Facebook Hateful Memes (FHM) and Bangla Hateful Memes (BHM) datasets, analyzing misclassifications to see if models over-index on or stereotype common target identity words (e.g., 'Islam', 'muslims', 'white', 'black').

Comparing zero-shot VLM performance on English meme datasets versus Bengali (BHM) and Hinglish datasets, demonstrating the models' monolingual limitations and inability to grasp regional cultural nuances or implicit cross-cultural hate.

Testing models on political and COVID-19-related harmful memes (HARM-P and HARM-C datasets) to assess their capability to detect harmful political satire, misinformation, and fake political conversations.
